To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
reference based indexing is a promising approach for similarity search, and that the reference selection and assignment methods that we propose outperform competitive methods.
1) our selection and assignment algorithms prune up to 30 times as much as frequency vectors and Omni, and 2) our algorithms scale nicely to large and/or long sequences.

the selection of a small set of references that serve as surrogates for the sequences in the database, and the assignment of references to the database sequences is a promising approach for similarity search in large databases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a reference based index to support similarity search in large sequence databases.
developing a reference based index for sequence similarity search that is both effective and scalable.
developing a reference based indexing method that can scale to very large databases and can be used for similarity search.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our method is the most promising method for similarity search in large databases.
the new methods are the most promising for the problem of similarity searching in very large sequence databases.
the proposed reference based index is an effective tool for similarity search in very large sequence databases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our methods are the best reference based methods to date.
our reference based indexing methods can be very efficient for answering queries with edit distance as a similarity measure.
reference based indexing is a promising approach to large sequence similarity search.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a good selection of references can be very effective in pruning the search space, even when the references are assigned to sequences in a simple and inexpensive way.
a small amount of additional information about the database can significantly improve the performance of reference based indices.
a small number of well-chosen references can significantly reduce the number of edit distance computations required for answering a query, even when the database contains many very long sequences.
